Subject: Request: mid-term GPU top-up and pricing options

Hi Evelyn / Marcus,

We need to scope an urgent top-up of our Dedicated GPU pool tied to the HZN-2391 contract. Over the last two weeks our inference traffic spiked (new patient triage feature) and we're short on throughput. Specifically, we want to add 8 A100-equivalent GPUs for an initial 3-month window starting Sept 1, with the option to convert to a longer reserve at renewal.

Questions we need answered quickly:
- Pricing for an immediate 3-month add-on (per-GPU monthly and blended rates)
- Is there an elastic/committed baseline + burst model you offer (we don't want to pay full commit for sustained baseline + occasional peaks)
- Throughput guarantees and what SLA credits would look like if p99 latency rises during bursts
- Do you provide pro-rated credits if we convert the top-up into a long-term commit mid-term?

Attaching the current PO/contract ref in body (contract ID HZN-2391). Can you send a draft quote and a recommended option by EOD next Tuesday (2026-08-10)?

Subject: Draft: pricing options for 3-month top-up (HZN-2391)

Tom / Evelyn — attaching a short draft quote and worksheet. Summary of the options we recommend:

Option A — Immediate Add-on (simple)
- Add 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs to your Dedicated pool for a fixed 3-month term.
- List price: $13,500 / GPU / month (A100 equiv).
- Total (3 months): $13,500 * 8 * 3 = $324,000.

Option B — Elastic Commit (recommended for spiky workloads)
- Baseline commit: reserve 4 GPUs (billed monthly at committed rate).
- Burstable pool: ability to burst up to +4 GPUs when demand requires, billed at a reduced burst rate.
- Blended effective rate (example): baseline rate $11,000/GPU/mo + burst consumption charged at $0.60/min equivalent; estimated blended cost for typical spike pattern: ~$280,000 over 3 months.
- We can offer a 10% discount on baseline commit for a 6-month agreed follow-up.

Option C — On-demand hour-based top-up
- Hourly pool at $6.50 / GPU-hour. Good for very short, predictable peaks but more expensive if used continuously.

Throughput / SLA notes:
- Baseline (committed) guarantees: p99 inference latency <= 250ms for seq length <= 512 under the provisioned throughput.
- During burst periods there is higher variance; we propose an SLA schedule where credits apply if p99 > 400ms for >5% of minutes in a billing month. Credit formula is 1% bill credit per 30 minutes over the threshold, capped at 20%.

Attached: HZN-2391-draft-quote.pdf (summary pricing), elastic-commit-worksheet.xlsx (cost model).

Next steps: Tom — confirm which option you'd like priced firm; Evelyn / Priyom: I'll update the draft quote based on the option and the discount ask.

Subject: Re: Draft: pricing options for 3-month top-up (HZN-2391) — elastic commit mechanics

Tom — quick breakdown on the elastic commit mechanics and the answers to your two asks.

1) Discount: we can accommodate 12% baseline discount if you commit to the conversion clause (conversion means pro-rated credit of the 3-month baseline already paid will be applied against the 12-month reserve on day-one of the new term). We'll reflect that in the amendment.

2) Unused commit handling:
- Monthly roll-forward credit: up to 30% of unused committed GPU-hours may be rolled forward month-over-month for up to two months (use it or lose it beyond that).
- Pro-rate on conversion: any remaining unused committed hours at conversion will be converted to dollar credit against the new 12-month commit.
- We do bill committed baseline even if unused (commit is to reserve capacity); credits are the remediation rather than a full refund.

Throughput SLA detail (excerpt):
- Baseline guarantee: p99 <= 250ms for seq <= 512 at provisioned throughput (measured at the customer token ingress).
- Burst behavior: burst requests are queued to burst pool; p95 generally preserved, p99 may be elevated. If p99 > 400ms for >5% of minutes in a billing month, Redwood will apply SLA credit per appendix. Appendix attached (throughput-sla-appendix.pdf).

Sample math (example month):
- Baseline: 4 GPUs reserved -> billed at committed rate.
- Burst consumption: 1200 burst GPU-hours that month charged at burst rate -> ~$720 (example).
- If convert to 12-month reserve in month 3, any unused baseline hours are pro-rated to credit against the 12-month invoice.

Attaching: elastic-commit-worksheet.xlsx (worked example), throughput-sla-appendix.pdf (SLA language).

If this matches procurement needs I'll ask Marcus / Evelyn to issue the updated draft quote + DocuSign amendment.
